title: A message today. A moment to come back to.
narration: This is Time Capsule: a Twitch chat experience that saves predictions now and reveals them together on a future stream. This walkthrough uses your real build screenshots, from the first server to the complete demo.
bullets: Streamer, viewer, moderator and OBS flows

title: Start the local app
narration: Phase one starts in the time capsule project inside WSL. Use Linux Node and npm, install the dependencies, and start the development server. Keep that terminal running while using the dashboard or OBS overlay.
code:
cd ~/hackathon_projects/time-capsule
export PATH="$PWD/.tools/node/bin:$PATH"
npm ci
npm run dev

title: Confirm the foundation
narration: Open localhost, port three thousand, slash health. An okay response confirms the server and SQLite database are available. The current build reports phase eight. Tests, type checking, lint, and build checks verify the foundation and later phases.

title: Register the Twitch application
narration: In the Twitch Developer Console, register a confidential Chat Bot application. Set the callback to localhost, port three thousand, slash auth slash callback, exactly. Put the client credentials in the local environment file, then restart the app.

title: Connect your streamer account
narration: Open the private dashboard link printed by the server and connect the streamer account. Your screenshot confirms romilg16 is connected and ready to moderate. One account is enough; a separate bot is optional and must be a channel moderator.

title: Listen to live channel events
narration: Phase three connects Twitch EventSub and live dashboard updates. Your screenshot shows EventSub connected and a received chat event. This confirms messages can travel from Twitch into the local application, even while the channel is offline.

title: Send a viewer message
narration: From a second Twitch account, open the streamer channel and send a simple message. Here, romil100 sends hi in romilg16’s chat. Match it with the dashboard event to check the correct channel and viewer identity.
bullets: Match the message with the event log

title: Check the capsule command
narration: Now send exclamation capsule. With no capsule accepting messages, the bot replies that no capsule is open for sealing. That is the correct response and verifies both command handling and outbound chat before creating a capsule.
bullets: Bot replies in the same channel
No active capsule is an expected state

title: Choose a capsule title and limits
narration: Phase four adds capsule creation and sealing. Give the capsule a clear title, choose its opening condition, and set viewer limits. This example uses Test predictions, three messages per viewer, and a maximum length of two hundred and eighty characters.

title: Create the capsule
narration: Click Create capsule. The new card should show Sealing and a sealed-message count. Only one capsule accepts new seals at a time. Lock or archive that capsule before creating another; locked capsules preserve their existing messages.
bullets: Public link is separate from the dashboard
One capsule collects seals at a time

title: Seal from another account
narration: From the viewer account, send exclamation seal followed by a prediction. The app saves and numbers it, attempts to delete the original chat message, and sends a receipt. Your screenshot shows message one sealed and the viewer message removed.
bullets: !seal I predict we will win the next round

title: Inspect the public capsule page
narration: The public page shows the title, opening condition, sealed count, and instructions for viewers. It does not show private message contents. Validation also enforces message length, blocked words, cooldowns, and the configured per-viewer limit.

title: A ready capsule still waits for a live stream
narration: Phase five adds automatic opening conditions and manual controls. Open now can override the chosen condition, but opening still requires a live stream. Your offline screenshot correctly shows Ready, waiting for the next live stream.
bullets: Manual opening respects the live gate
Settling delay runs once the stream is live

title: Postpone without losing the seals
narration: Postpone delays the opening by ten minutes while preserving the capsule’s messages and original condition. The dashboard displays the new deadline. The live-stream requirement still applies, so an offline channel does not reveal anything accidentally.
bullets: Wait for the deadline and a live stream

title: Use the right opening condition
narration: The four opening choices are manual, a date, a follower goal, or the first stream in a selected category. Your GTA 6 capsule was configured for Grand Theft Auto Three. The displayed category, rather than the title, controls this trigger.
bullets: Category matching uses the category ID
Title and opening category are independent

title: Archive is a different action
narration: Archiving preserves existing seals and stops that capsule’s normal workflow. In your screenshot, Test predictions is archived while GTA 6 is still sealing. Archiving a capsule does not start a Twitch broadcast; streaming is controlled separately in OBS.
bullets: Another capsule may still be SEALING
OBS starts the actual Twitch stream

title: Connect OBS to Twitch
narration: In OBS Settings, open Stream and choose Twitch. Connect the streamer account and keep the recommended automatic server. Your screenshot shows the account connected. Leave bandwidth test mode off when the goal is a real live test.

title: Check Twitch Stream Manager
narration: Open Twitch Stream Manager for romilg16 to monitor the broadcast. Before OBS starts transmitting, Offline is expected. The stream preview, chat, activity feed, and stream information help confirm that OBS is using the intended channel.

title: Keep the local dashboard running
narration: Keep the Time Capsule server and dashboard open during the test. The opening checks show the live state, follower count, and category. This screenshot is still offline, so the capsule is waiting even though opening controls are visible.

title: Set stream information
narration: In OBS Stream Information, enter a title such as Time Capsule test and select the category required by your capsule. Click Done to save. A stream title describes the broadcast; the category is a separate field used by the category trigger.
bullets: Click Done to save stream information

title: Choose accurate stream labels
narration: The Rerun checkbox is for previously recorded broadcasts. Branded Content applies when that stream actually includes the commercial relationships described by Twitch. Choose labels that match your broadcast; a mature-game category may add its own locked content label.

title: Start the broadcast in OBS
narration: After saving stream information, use Start Streaming in the OBS Controls panel. Your next screenshot shows Stop Streaming, confirming OBS started sending. Watch the status bar and check Stream Manager for a live broadcast.

title: A black preview needs a source
narration: A black stream does not mean you must play a game. OBS needs a visible source to capture. Your Twitch screenshot shows a live but black preview, with an unstable connection indicator. Source visibility and connection stability are separate checks.
bullets: A game is optional for this test

title: Add Window Capture
narration: Use the plus button under Sources and add Window Capture. Select a safe window, such as a terminal without credentials, and fit it to the canvas. Your OBS screenshot shows the terminal capture active while the camera source is hidden.
bullets: Fit the source to the canvas

title: Confirm the stream receives video
narration: The Twitch preview now shows the captured terminal, so OBS is sending visible content. Keep the chosen category aligned with the capsule condition, and wait for the opening delay. The app can test this workflow without requiring actual gameplay.
bullets: Wait for the configured opening delay

title: An empty ceremony has nothing to reveal
narration: Phase six adds the opening ceremony and moderation queue. Your first GTA 6 test had zero messages, so Reveal next and auto-reveal were disabled. End ceremony is appropriate after testing an empty queue; the capsule and its decisions remain saved.

title: The overlay is a Browser Source
narration: The Time Capsule overlay is not a built-in OBS dock. Add it as a Browser Source from the Sources panel. Your screenshot still shows only Window Capture and the camera, so the overlay needs its own source above them.
bullets: Place it above the capture sources

title: Copy the private OBS URL
narration: Scroll to Your OBS overlay in the dashboard and copy its Browser Source URL. Use the overlay link, not the dashboard or public page. The monitor’s checkerboard represents transparency. The ten-second preview uses sample cards and does not change your capsules.
bullets: Copy OBS URL from the dashboard
Keep the private URL out of broadcasts

title: Configure the Browser Source
narration: Paste the complete overlay URL into the OBS Browser Source. Set the width to nineteen twenty and the height to ten eighty. The screenshot shows ten seventy-nine, so correct that field. Disable shutting down hidden sources and refreshing the browser when the scene becomes active.
bullets: Paste the complete private overlay URL
Keep the source alive between scenes

title: A transparent idle overlay is expected
narration: You do not need to open the overlay in a separate browser first. OBS loads it directly. Outside a ceremony or preview, it is intentionally empty and transparent. With every background source hidden, that transparent canvas looks black.

title: Approve before revealing
narration: Once a capsule opens, review its private moderation queue. Approve messages you want to show and reject anything unsuitable. This screenshot has one approved message and no pending messages, so the Pending filter looks empty. Change the filter to inspect approved entries.
bullets: Reveal next or press N outside a field

title: Control the opening ceremony
narration: Use Reveal next for one approved card, or Start auto-reveal for timed progression. Press N only when you are not typing into a field. Overlay settings control card side, size, and interval. End ceremony clears the cards and preserves the review history.
bullets: Card side, size and reveal interval
code:
SEALED
  ↓ opening condition + live stream
PRIVATE MODERATION QUEUE
  ↓ approve
REVEAL ON OBS
  ↓ end ceremony
EMPTY, TRANSPARENT OVERLAY

title: Create a Prophet VIP test capsule
narration: Phase seven recognizes predictions that come true. Create a new capsule called Prophet VIP Test, choose a manual opening for testing, and enable Reward Prophets with VIP if you want to test the role reward. This example uses thirty days.

title: Send the prediction as a viewer
narration: From the separate viewer account, send exclamation seal followed by the prediction. Here, romil100’s message is removed and the bot confirms sealed message one. Broadcaster and moderator messages cannot always be hidden, which is why a normal viewer account is useful.
bullets: Wait for the numbered bot receipt

title: Open the test capsule while live
narration: With the stream live, click Open now and wait through the delay and opening animation. The capsule changes to Opening and directs you to the ceremony controls. Approve the saved prediction, then reveal it before trying to mark it true.

title: Mark a revealed prediction true
narration: In Prophets, mark the revealed prediction Came true only when it actually happened. This saves the recognition, adds the Prophet badge and Came True stamp to the overlay, and attempts the optional reward. Your OBS screenshot shows the recognition working.

title: Confirm the chat announcement
narration: The bot also announces the Prophet in Twitch chat. Your screenshot confirms romil100’s prediction came true. The announcement and overlay recognition are separate from VIP eligibility, so those can succeed even when Twitch refuses a role reward.

title: If the overlay vanishes, check the eye icon
narration: This OBS screenshot shows the Browser Source hidden while Window Capture is visible. Click the crossed-out eye beside Browser to show it, and keep it above the capture source. A working overlay cannot appear in the broadcast while its source is hidden.
bullets: Keep the capture source visible below

title: Read the real VIP result honestly
narration: The real Twitch test returned No free VIP slots. The prediction still became a Prophet and the chat announcement succeeded, but VIP was not granted. Free a slot if the channel is eligible, then use Retry VIP. Never treat this error as a successful grant.
bullets: Real test: no free VIP slots
Resolve the issue, then Retry VIP

title: End the ceremony and preserve the result
narration: End ceremony returns the overlay to empty and transparent. Your dashboard keeps the prediction, recognition, and VIP error for review. The app checks reward expiry at startup and hourly, and only removes temporary VIP roles it owns; existing VIPs are preserved.
bullets: Owned VIP rewards expire; existing VIPs remain

title: Visit the Wall of Prophets
narration: Open the capsule’s public page after the ceremony. Your screenshot shows romil100 on the Wall of Prophets with one prediction that came true. The public view shows display names and counts, while private message contents and reward-management details remain in the dashboard.
bullets: No private message text on the public page

title: Try it without a Twitch account
narration: Phase eight adds a completely separate account-free demo. Run npm run demo and open the printed URL. It uses fictional Twitch accounts, fresh demo storage, and fake messages and VIP roles. Your real capsule database and connected account are not used.

title: Play the full ninety-second story
narration: Click Play full story. Twenty sample viewers seal predictions, a week of simulated time passes, the stream goes live, and the category changes. The production trigger and ceremony services open the capsule, reveal three approved highlights, and award one fake VIP.
bullets: One Came true → fake VIP → clear overlay
code:
00:03–00:22   20 viewers seal
00:26        Lock sealing
00:30        Advance simulated time
00:38        Go live
00:45        Change category
00:58        Approve messages
01:00–01:08   Reveal highlights
01:12        Came true + fake VIP
01:22–01:30   End and complete

title: Explore the manual demo controls
narration: You can also create category, date, or follower-goal demo capsules. Send sample seals, fast-forward the date, go live, or reach a thousand followers. Stop the automatic story before using manual controls. The date scenario correctly waits offline until the simulated stream goes live.
bullets: Fake events use the real app workflow

title: Verify EventSub with the Twitch CLI
narration: For a separate socket test, start the Twitch CLI mock WebSocket server, then run npm run test colon CLI. Trigger a version two channel update for fictional broadcaster ten thousand and one. The client should report the matching category notification. This does not contact your real channel.
code:
twitch event websocket start-server --require-subscription

npm run test:cli

twitch event trigger channel.update \
  --transport=websocket --version=2 \
  --to-user=10001 --game-id=900000001 \
  --item-name="Grand Theft Auto VI"

title: From the first server to the full story
narration: All eight completed phases are covered: the server, authentication, live events, sealing, opening triggers, OBS ceremonies, Prophet rewards, and the isolated demo. The build passed one hundred and ninety-three tests, type checking, lint, and compilation. Phase nine remains future polish.
bullets: Seal today. Reveal when it matters.
code:
01  Foundation        05  Opening triggers
02  Twitch auth       06  Ceremony + OBS
03  EventSub + chat   07  Prophets + VIP
04  Capsules + seals  08  Account-free demo
